task: compose and send an email in a mail client (Gmail, Outlook, Yahoo Mail, Apple Mail): open compose, address the recipient, write the subject and body, optionally attach a file, send it, and verify it in Sent; complete when the message shows as sent. Surface pinned: the mail client's compose-and-send flow — not inbox-organizing tours, not newsletter/marketing tools, not email-etiquette advice videos.

tree.label: Send an email
tree.note: 1 when the client is not already open and signed in - most keepers start authenticated and skip most of it. then 2: a new message, or a reply or forward entered from 8.1 (DFXu, ycKB, 6rzA, 0D7H, zCsj), which decides how much of 3 is left to do. 3 and 4 in either order - HnFK writes the subject and body before the recipient. 5 where the message carries a file; 5.4 only when the client refuses the file, and it returns into 5.2 or 5.5 once the file is ready (UehN never gets back). then 6, one of 6.2 to 6.5; 6.6 and 6.7 where the client interrupts. then 7 - in this corpus that's where the task actually completes, and 7 is skipped by seven keepers. 8 at any point.

children.label: Get into the mailbox
children.note: 1.1 then 1.2. 1.3 only from a logged-out start - two keepers. 1.4 where more than one account is signed in. 1.5 and 1.6 as orientation before any composing, and only on the videos that tour the client.

questions.question: Should you enable high priority notifications or dismiss the prompt by tapping 'No thanks'?
questions.why: The inbox displays a banner offering to 'Try notifications for only your high priority emails' with options to 'Turn on' or say 'No thanks', which must be navigated or ignored to continue.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the chance to opt into or permanently dismiss a system-level notification preference for their inbox.
questions.check: Does the inbox show a banner offering to turn on notifications for high priority emails?
questions.say_example: Gmail offered a notification setting. I said no thanks and moved on.

questions.question: Which app do you open to access your email?
questions.why: The home screen displays multiple applications, so you must select the specific mail client you want to use to send the message.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to choose which specific email client or account is used to send the message.
questions.check: Which mail apps or icons does the screen show?
questions.say_example: Opened Gmail, where your account lives.

questions.question: The page is asking you to sign in — do you want to enter your password yourself?
questions.why: The sign-in screen requires an email and password, which can be typed manually or autofilled using a password manager.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to decide whether to securely autofill your credentials using a specific password manager or type them manually.
questions.check: Does the page show a sign-in form asking for an email or password?
questions.say_example: Gmail wants you to sign in. The password part is yours. I'll wait.

questions.question: Which email account are you currently sending from?
questions.why: Opening the profile pop-up reveals the active email address, '[email]', ensuring the message is sent from the correct account.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the opportunity to verify or switch their sender identity before composing the message.
questions.check: Which email address does the profile menu show as the active account?
questions.say_example: You're signed in as <address>. Everything goes out under that name.

children.label: Open a compose surface
children.note: 2.1 for a new message. 2.2 and 2.3 instead when the message answers one that arrived, entered from 8.1 - and that choice sets what 3 has left to do: reply-all arrives with To and Cc filled, forward arrives with To empty and quoted history attached. 2.4 after the draft exists. 2.5 where the compose surface is a panel that can be resized. 2.6 before typing, on the two keepers that tour the surface first.

questions.question: The compose window restored a stale previous draft - should it be discarded so the new email starts clean instead of appending to it?
questions.why: The screen shows the user clicking the 'Discard draft' trash can icon before clicking 'Compose' again, which is necessary to clear the stale state if the mail client automatically restores a previous, unfinished message.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the ability to ensure they are starting with a clean slate, risking the agent accidentally appending the new message to an old, irrelevant draft.
questions.check: Does the compose window show a restored draft with existing text in it?
questions.say_example: An old unfinished draft opened up. I'm leaving it saved and starting fresh.

questions.question: Did the forward open with the original message included?
questions.why: Clicking the 'Forward' link below the thread automatically populates a new compose window with the original message and a 'Fwd:' subject line.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to decide whether to forward the existing thread or summarize the information in a brand new email.
questions.check: Does the subject line start with 'Fwd:' and does the body contain the quoted original message?
questions.say_example: The forward opened empty. The original message didn't come along, so I'm redoing it before anything else.

questions.question: Should you change the response type to Reply, Reply All, or Forward?
questions.why: The screen shows a dropdown menu that lets you switch the current draft between a direct reply, a reply to all, or a forward.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to manually control exactly which participants from the original email thread will receive your message.
questions.check: How many recipients does the original thread show in its To and Cc fields?
questions.say_example: This thread has <four> people on it. Reply just to <Ted>, or to everyone?

children.label: Set the recipients
children.note: 3.1 in nearly every keeper - typing resolved by a suggestion is close to universal here. 3.2 where the address is not in the list. 3.3 to reach the copy fields, then 3.4 and 3.5 where the message needs them. 3.6 replaces all of it on a bulk send, and rules 3.3 to 3.5 out. 3.7 whenever a chip is wrong. 3.8 before trusting a group. reply-all routes arrive with this goal already done (DFXu).

questions.question: Did the email client display a visual warning or color change indicating that the recipient is outside your organization?
questions.why: Many corporate email clients visually flag external addresses (e.g., with a yellow banner or red text) to prevent accidental data leaks, a cue that must be explicitly read if not looking at the screen.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the immediate visual alert that they are about to send potentially sensitive information to an external contact.
questions.check: Does the compose window or send dialog show an external-recipient warning banner or tag?
questions.say_example: Heads up, <this address> is outside your company, and the client flagged it.

questions.question: This draft goes to several people as one message — one email to all, or a separate copy to each?
questions.why: The screen shows a single draft addressed to multiple recipients with a generic 'Hey' greeting, which prevents addressing each person by their actual name.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the personal touch of addressing each recipient by name, which makes the mass invitation feel less genuine.
questions.check: How many addresses are in the To field, and does the greeting name anyone?
questions.say_example: This goes to <three> people as one email, and they'll all see each other's addresses. One email to all, or separate copies?

questions.question: Which email address should you select as the recipient?
questions.why: The screen displays a list of multiple available email accounts, so you must select the correct one to ensure the message reaches the intended person.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this choice means the agent might select the wrong recipient from the list, potentially sending your message to an unintended contact.
questions.check: Which addresses does the suggestion dropdown show for the typed name?
questions.say_example: There are two <Sarah>s here, <sarah.j@...> and <sarah.k@...>. Which one?

questions.question: What exact email address are you entering in the 'To' field?
questions.why: Entering the precise email address in the 'To' field ensures the message reaches the correct person instead of bouncing or going to a stranger.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the chance to personally verify that the recipient's address is typed perfectly to avoid sending the message to the wrong person.
questions.check: What address does the To field show?
questions.say_example: The To field says <address>, which isn't the address you gave me. Fixing it.

questions.question: Did the client flag the recipient's address as invalid, either while typing or when the send failed?
questions.why: If an email address is missing an '@' symbol or a valid domain, the client usually flags it immediately with a visual error, preventing a failed send later.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the chance to catch and correct a structural typo in the email address before attempting to send the message.
questions.check: Does the To field show the address marked as an error, or did a send attempt fail with an invalid-address message?
questions.say_example: The client flagged <the address> as not a real address. Can you check it with me?

questions.question: Who should you add as a Cc recipient?
questions.why: The dropdown suggests contacts like 'Woggle Spy Lucinda' based on your typing, requiring you to select the correct person to keep in the loop.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this means you lose the ability to decide exactly who needs visibility into the conversation without being the primary recipient.
questions.check: Which addresses does the Cc field show?
questions.say_example: Cc'd <name>, as you asked.

questions.question: When replying to a thread, does the recipient list still include everyone from the original?
questions.why: Confirming that the visible names and the '+1' indicator match the three original Cc recipients ensures no one is accidentally dropped from the thread.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the assurance that all necessary stakeholders are kept in the loop on the communication.
questions.check: Which addresses are in the Cc field once the '+N' indicator is expanded, and which were on the original thread?
questions.say_example: <One> of the original people fell off this reply. <Name> isn't on it anymore. Add them back?

questions.question: Who should you blind carbon copy on this email?
questions.why: The screen shows an autocomplete dropdown with multiple contacts like Woggle Spy Cynthia and Woggle Spy Cuthbert for the Bcc field, requiring a choice of who should secretly receive the message.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this choice means the agent might blind copy the wrong contact, potentially failing to keep the right person confidentially informed.
questions.check: Which addresses does the Bcc field show?
questions.say_example: Bcc'd <name>, as you asked.

children.label: Build a bulk recipient list
children.note: 3.6.2 first - the feature has to be switched on before anything else changes. then 3.6.1, and one of 3.6.3 or the pair 3.6.4 and 3.6.5. 3.6.6 is read after the fact in this keeper, not before.

questions.question: Should you use the mail merge option to add recipients from a spreadsheet?
questions.why: Clicking the mail merge icon revealed a dropdown to add recipients from a spreadsheet, which fundamentally changes how the email is addressed.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the opportunity to decide whether to automate addressing a mass email using a spreadsheet or to enter recipients manually.
questions.check: Does the compose window show the mail merge option turned on?
questions.say_example: Using mail merge, since your list lives in the spreadsheet.

questions.question: Which contacts do you want to include in this mail merge?
questions.why: The 'Select contacts' modal offers individual selection or a 'Select All' option for the three available contacts.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to hand-pick exactly which of your contacts should receive the message.
questions.check: Which contacts does the selection modal show as checked?
questions.say_example: Selected all <three> contacts for the merge.

questions.question: Which spreadsheet contains the recipient data?
questions.why: The screen showed a 'Link a spreadsheet for recipient info' dialog displaying recent files like 'School Fees', requiring a choice of data source.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses control over which contact list is used, risking sending the email to the wrong group of people.
questions.check: Which files does the link-a-spreadsheet dialog list?
questions.say_example: Two sheets look like the fee list, <School Fees> and <School Fees (1)>. Which one is current?

questions.question: Which columns from the spreadsheet will you use to personalize the email?
questions.why: Reviewing the 'School Fees' sheet ensures you know exactly which fields, like 'Amount Due' and 'Account Number', are available to insert into the message.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this means you lose the opportunity to manually verify that the data source contains all the necessary and correct fields before generating the emails.
questions.check: Which column names does the linked spreadsheet show?
questions.say_example: The sheet has <Amount Due> and <Account Number> to fill from.

questions.question: Did the client block or warn about the send because of an account sending limit?
questions.why: Gmail restricts standard accounts to 500 outgoing messages and mail merge to 1,500 recipients per day, meaning exceeding these limits will block your emails from sending.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the awareness of your account's specific sending thresholds, which could result in a blocked campaign if the agent blindly exceeds the limit.
questions.check: Does the page show a message that a sending limit was reached or that the message was blocked?
questions.say_example: Gmail stopped the batch. It says the account hit its sending limit, so the rest won't go out today.

questions.question: Does the page say mail merge disables a feature this message needs, like Cc or scheduling?
questions.why: The help page explicitly states that using a spreadsheet for mail merge prevents you from adding Cc or Bcc recipients and disables features like schedule send and confidential mode.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to weigh whether the convenience of a spreadsheet outweighs the need to copy other recipients or schedule the email.
questions.check: Does the page state that mail merge cannot be used with Cc, Bcc, scheduled send, or confidential mode?
questions.say_example: Merge mode can't Cc anyone, the page says so. Separate copies without the Cc, or one plain email with it?

questions.question: Is the intended contact group available to select in the dropdown?
questions.why: Seeing the 'Test Group' entry with its member count in the autocomplete dropdown confirms the mail client recognizes your pre-made distribution list.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this means you cannot visually verify the group's member count to ensure the exact right list of people will receive your message.
questions.check: Does the suggestion dropdown show the group name with a member count?
questions.say_example: I can't find a group called <Test Group> in your contacts. Want me to add people one by one?

questions.question: Who does the contact group actually expand to?
questions.why: Checking the details pane for 'Test Group' ensures you know exactly which email addresses, like Christian and Dad, will receive the message.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the peace of mind of manually reviewing and confirming the exact individuals included in a group alias before the email goes out.
questions.check: Which member addresses does the group's detail view list?
questions.say_example: The <Test Group> chip is <two> people, <Christian> and <Dad>. That's who gets it.

children.label: Write the message
children.note: 4.1 then 4.2 - HnFK does both before the recipient. 4.3 where the client suggests text mid-typing. 4.4 only where the content comes from another application. 4.5 on a forward, before the quoted history travels with it. 4.6 once per field the spreadsheet supplies. 4.7 is opened in three keepers and applied in one.

questions.question: What date, time, and duration should you set for the scheduled meeting?
questions.why: The 'Schedule Meeting' window requires you to configure the 'Topic', 'Start' date and time, and 'Duration' to generate the correct invitation details.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the control to pick a specific date and time that perfectly aligns with your unwritten scheduling preferences.
questions.check: What topic, start time, and duration does the schedule dialog show?
questions.say_example: Set the meeting for <Friday at 2>, <45 minutes>, like you said.

questions.question: Should I use your Personal Meeting ID or generate one automatically, and do you want to require a password?
questions.why: The screen shows options to either generate a meeting ID automatically or use a Personal Meeting ID, along with a checkbox to require a meeting password.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the ability to balance convenience and security for their specific meeting participants.
questions.check: Which meeting ID option is selected, and is the password box checked?
questions.say_example: Generated a fresh meeting ID rather than exposing your personal one, and left the password on.

questions.question: Should I enable video for the host and participants?
questions.why: The screen showed radio buttons to toggle video on or off for the host and participants, which sets the default camera behavior for the integrated meeting.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the ability to dictate the meeting's visual engagement and privacy boundaries based on their relationship with the attendees.
questions.check: Which video options are selected for host and participants?
questions.say_example: Video is set to off for people joining. They can turn it on themselves.

questions.question: Which audio options do you want to allow for the meeting?
questions.why: The screen displayed radio buttons to choose between Telephone, Computer Audio, or both for the meeting details being added to the email.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The delegator loses the ability to specify how recipients are allowed to dial into or connect to the meeting.
questions.check: Which audio option is selected in the dialog?
questions.say_example: Allowed both phone and computer audio, the widest option.

questions.question: Which calendar system should you select for scheduling?
questions.why: The screen presents radio buttons for Outlook, Google Calendar, and Other Calendars, requiring a choice for the scheduling integration.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the ability to ensure the scheduling tool aligns with their preferred personal or corporate calendar ecosystem.
questions.check: Which calendar option is selected in the dialog?
questions.say_example: Picked Google Calendar, where your calendar lives.

questions.question: Do you want to enable any advanced meeting settings, such as allowing participants to join before the host?
questions.why: The screen showed a collapsed 'Advanced Options' menu containing specific settings for waiting rooms, early joining, and automatic recording.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the ability to control the specific entry and recording behaviors for their meeting attendees.
questions.check: Which advanced options are checked in the expanded menu?
questions.say_example: Left the advanced options alone. The waiting room stays on.

questions.question: Do you need to edit or delete the auto-inserted email signature for this specific message?
questions.why: Mail clients often automatically append a default signature to the bottom of the message body, which you might want to remove for casual replies or edit to hide a phone number.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the ability to tailor their sign-off and control what personal contact information is shared in the specific context of this email.
questions.check: Does the draft end with the default signature block?
questions.say_example: Left your usual signature on.

questions.question: Should you mark the message with 'High Importance' or flag it for 'Follow Up'?
questions.why: The Outlook message ribbon contains explicit buttons for 'High Importance' and 'Follow Up' that alter how the email is presented and tracked.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the ability to explicitly signal the urgency of the message to the recipient or set a reminder for themselves.
questions.check: Are the High Importance or Follow Up buttons active on the draft?
questions.say_example: Didn't mark it high importance. You didn't ask for that.

questions.question: Is your default email signature correctly positioned at the bottom of the draft without being accidentally deleted or duplicated?
questions.why: Automated agents or careless pasting can easily overwrite the pre-filled default signature or paste a second one, making the email look unprofessional.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the assurance that their standard professional sign-off and contact information are intact and properly formatted.
questions.check: How many copies of the signature block does the draft contain, and is one at the bottom?
questions.say_example: Your signature ended up in there twice. I removed the extra one.

questions.question: What should you enter as the subject of the email?
questions.why: The screen shows an empty 'Subject:' field that requires a concise summary of the email's purpose.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to craft a specific subject line that sets the right tone and context for your recipient.
questions.check: What does the Subject field contain?
questions.say_example: Subject's in: <Fees due Friday>.

questions.question: What do you want to write in the message body?
questions.why: The 'Compose email' field is where the actual content and details of your message must be entered.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this step means you lose control over the exact wording, tone, and specific details communicated to the recipient.
questions.check: What text does the message body contain?
questions.say_example: The message is drafted, all from what you told me.

questions.question: Should you interact with the Smart Compose tooltip or ignore it and type your message manually?
questions.why: The screen displays a Smart Compose tooltip offering writing suggestions that can be acknowledged, disabled, or simply ignored while drafting.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this means you lose the choice of whether to utilize, dismiss, or permanently disable the AI writing suggestions for your account.
questions.check: Is a Smart Compose suggestion showing in the body?
questions.say_example: Ignored the grey autocomplete text. Every word stays yours.

questions.question: Do you want to use the 'Help me write' AI options to formalize, elaborate, or shorten your draft?
questions.why: The compose window displays a 'Help me write' menu with options like 'Formalize', 'Elaborate', and 'Shorten' that can automatically rewrite the text you entered.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the ability to decide whether to rely on AI to adjust the tone and length of their message or to send their own exact words.
questions.check: Does the compose window show the 'Help me write' menu?
questions.say_example: Skipped the 'Help me write' button. The words stay yours.

questions.question: Do the generated meeting invitation details read back correctly before they are copied into the email?
questions.why: The 'Zoom - Schedule Meeting' dialog offers options to open with a default calendar or copy to the clipboard.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the opportunity to review the meeting details before they are copied and sent.
questions.check: Does the dialog offer a copy-to-clipboard option for the meeting details?
questions.say_example: Copied the meeting details into the message.

questions.question: Should you keep or delete the forwarded email history below your new message?
questions.why: The screen shows the previous email thread appended below the new message, which might clutter the email or include unnecessary context.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to curate the email's context and ensure the recipient only sees the relevant information you intended to share.
questions.check: Does the draft contain the quoted earlier messages below the new text, and how many?
questions.say_example: The whole old thread rides along under your note, <five> earlier messages. Keep the history, or send just your part?

questions.question: Which merge tag do you want to use for the greeting?
questions.why: The screen shows a menu of mail merge tags like '@ firstname' and '@ lastname', which determines how the recipient's name will be formatted in the automated greeting.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The delegator loses control over the tone of the email by not being able to choose between a casual first name or a more formal full name greeting.
questions.check: Which merge tags does the tag menu show?
questions.say_example: Used the first-name tag for the greeting.

questions.question: Are all the purple placeholder tags correctly positioned in your draft?
questions.why: Verifying the purple highlight tags like '@firstname' and '@amountdue' ensures the mail merge will populate the correct data for each recipient before you click Continue.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to personally verify that sensitive merge fields like account numbers and amounts due are placed in the correct context within the message.
questions.check: Does each placeholder in the body render as a live tag chip rather than plain text?
questions.say_example: One placeholder isn't live. <@amountdue> is sitting there as plain text, so everyone would see those literal words instead of their amount. Fixing it.

questions.question: Does the pasted text contain broken formatting or unreadable background colors that need to be cleared?
questions.why: Pasting content from external documents or websites often imports incompatible HTML formatting, making the email look broken or unprofessional.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The ability to notice and strip out corrupted rich-text formatting before the recipient sees a garbled message.
questions.check: Does the pasted text carry a background color or font different from the rest of the body?
questions.say_example: The pasted part came in with a white box behind it and a different font. I cleared the formatting so it reads as one message.

children.label: Attach a file
children.note: 5.1 opens the source list, and which sources exist is the client's decision, not the user's. then 5.2, or 5.3 where the file is dragged in instead, or 5.5 where it lives in cloud storage. 5.4 fires when the client refuses what was picked, and returns into 5.2 or 5.5 once the file is ready. 5.6 where the upload has to finish before anything else. three keepers open 5.1 and attach nothing at all.

questions.question: Do you need to attach any files or Drive links to this email?
questions.why: The compose toolbar displays icons for attaching local files or inserting from Google Drive, prompting a choice about including supplementary documents.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this step means you lose the ability to judge whether additional context or specific documents should accompany your message.
questions.check: Does the draft show any attachment chips?
questions.say_example: Attached <the file>, as you asked.

questions.question: Which source should you select from the Attach File dropdown?
questions.why: The dropdown offers recent items, web locations, and the local PC, so you must specify where the intended file is currently stored.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to decide exactly which storage location to pull the attachment from, risking the selection of an incorrect or outdated version of the file.
questions.check: Which sources does the Attach File dropdown list?
questions.say_example: Grabbing the file from <this PC>, where you said it lives.

questions.question: Which file do you select to attach to the email?
questions.why: Choosing the correct file from the Downloads folder ensures the intended image, such as 'Cool Guy.jpg', is attached to the email.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the opportunity to manually browse your folders and visually verify you are attaching the exact file you intended.
questions.check: Which file names does the picker show matching what the person asked for?
questions.say_example: Two files are called <resume>, one from <March>, one from <yesterday>. Which one?

questions.question: Can the file you asked for be found where you said it was?
questions.why: The file manager displays multiple image directories like Camera, Downloads, and Canva, so you must know exactly where the intended attachment is saved.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this means losing the ability to visually browse your personal folders to find the exact image you intended to share.
questions.check: Does the picker show a file matching the requested name in the expected folder?
questions.say_example: I can't find <the file> where you said it would be. Where should I look?

questions.question: Does the picker's selected count match the number of files you meant to attach?
questions.why: The top bar explicitly shows '3 selected', requiring a tap on the 'Select' button to finalize adding them to the email.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to personally verify that the correct documents or images are being attached before they are added to the draft.
questions.check: What count does the picker's selection bar show?
questions.say_example: The picker says <2> selected but you asked for <3> files. One didn't take. Checking which.

questions.question: Should you grant the app permission to access all your photos?
questions.why: The system dialog requires you to choose whether to give the app access to all your photos, select specific ones, or deny access entirely.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the opportunity to protect your privacy by restricting the app's access to only specific photos rather than your entire library.
questions.check: Does a system dialog ask for photo access, and what scope options does it offer?
questions.say_example: The mail app wants access to your photos. That's all of them, not just this one, and it stays on afterward. There's an option for just the photos you pick. Which do you want?

questions.question: Do you want to resize the inline image?
questions.why: The screen shows options like 'Small' and 'Best fit' to control how the inline image appears within the email body.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the chance to visually verify the image's layout and choose the best fit for the recipient's reading experience.
questions.check: Which size option is selected for the inline image?
questions.say_example: Left the picture at best fit.

children.label: Prepare the file elsewhere
children.note: 5.4.1 names what stopped it. then whichever of 5.4.2 to 5.4.5 the block calls for: a folder gets compressed, an oversized file gets uploaded, a cloud file gets its sharing set, a cloud file that has to travel as bytes gets downloaded first. 5.4.6 where the client is not connected to the storage service at all. 5.4.3 after any compression. then back into 5.2 or 5.5 - UehN is the one keeper that never gets back.

questions.question: Can you attach an entire folder directly to the email?
questions.why: Selecting a folder and clicking 'Open' in the file browser merely opens it to reveal contents like 'road-259815_1280.jpg' rather than attaching the folder itself.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the awareness that folders cannot be attached directly and must either be zipped or have their individual files selected.
questions.check: Does selecting the folder in the picker open it rather than attach it?
questions.say_example: Email can't take a whole folder. I'll zip it into one file and attach that.

questions.question: Did the email client reject the attachment and display a security warning about a restricted file type?
questions.why: Mail clients actively block certain file extensions (like .exe, .bat, or scripts) for security, requiring the user to find an alternative sharing method like a cloud link.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the awareness that their specific file type is prohibited and will fail to attach, requiring a change in delivery strategy.
questions.check: Does the page show a blocked-attachment message naming the file type?
questions.say_example: The client refused the file. It blocks <.exe> attachments. I can share it as a Drive link instead. Want that?

questions.question: Do you want to use Mail Drop to send this oversized attachment?
questions.why: The attachment is 56.3 MB, which exceeds the 52.4 MB limit, prompting Apple Mail to offer iCloud delivery.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the opportunity to choose whether your file is temporarily hosted on iCloud or sent directly through your email provider.
questions.check: Does the page show a size-limit dialog, and what does it say the limit and the file size are?
questions.say_example: The file's too big to attach, <56 MB> against a <52 MB> limit. The client offers to send it as a cloud link instead. OK with that?

questions.question: Which folder needs to be compressed?
questions.why: The screen shows a File Explorer window with 'Folder To Be Emailed', which must be selected and compressed before it can be attached.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the ability to specify exactly which folder should be prepared and attached to the email.
questions.check: Which folder is selected in the file window?
questions.say_example: Zipping <the folder> you pointed me at.

questions.question: Is the option to compress the folder available in this context menu?
questions.why: The context menu for the Zoom folder lacks a compress or zip option, which is necessary because most email clients require folders to be zipped before attaching.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the ability to decide whether to troubleshoot the missing compression tool or simply abandon this folder and attach a different one.
questions.check: Does the context menu show a compress or zip option?
questions.say_example: No zip option on this menu, so I went another route.

questions.question: Is the folder you want to send empty?
questions.why: The screen shows an error dialog because the system cannot zip an empty directory, halting your attempt to prepare the attachment.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the chance to realize they forgot to put their intended files into the folder before trying to attach it to the email.
questions.check: Does an error dialog say the folder is empty or cannot be compressed?
questions.say_example: The folder you wanted to send is empty. There's nothing in it. Is that the right folder?

questions.question: Are these the correct files to compress and attach?
questions.why: The screen showed the contents of 'Folder To Be Emailed', allowing verification of the files before zipping them for the email.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the visual confirmation that all intended files are present in the folder before it gets compressed and sent.
questions.check: Which file names does the folder show before compressing?
questions.say_example: Zipping <ten> files, mostly photos, <8 MB> in all. The recipient only sees inside after unzipping, so say if something's in there that shouldn't be.

questions.question: Is there a new .zip file where the folder was?
questions.why: Confirming the completion notification and locating the new .zip file in the directory ensures the folder is actually ready to be attached.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the visual reassurance of seeing the newly created .zip file appear in your directory before it gets attached.
questions.check: Does the folder now contain a .zip file with the expected name?
questions.say_example: The zip never got created. Trying again before we go on.

questions.question: Do you want to rename the newly created ZIP file?
questions.why: The text 'Folder To Be Emailed' is highlighted in an editable text box, giving you the immediate option to customize the file name before attaching it.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the opportunity to apply a specific or more professional naming convention to the attachment that the recipient will see.
questions.check: What name does the new .zip file show?
questions.say_example: Kept the zip named after the folder. That's the name the recipient sees.

questions.question: Should you allow the browser to upload the entire folder?
questions.why: The browser explicitly asks if you trust the site before allowing the upload of all 10 files from the selected folder.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the opportunity to personally assess the security warning and explicitly grant the site access to your local files.
questions.check: Does the browser dialog say how many files will be uploaded and to which site?
questions.say_example: The browser wanted a yes before uploading all <10> files to <the site>. That matches what we're doing, so I confirmed.

questions.question: Is the file you want to attach already uploaded to your Google Drive?
questions.why: The Google Drive file picker displayed 'No files found,' indicating that the file must be uploaded to Drive first before it can be attached.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the ability to manually locate their local file and upload it to Drive when the agent gets stuck on an empty file picker.
questions.check: Does the Drive picker show the file, or does it say no files found?
questions.say_example: That file isn't in your Drive yet. I'll upload it first, then attach it.

questions.question: Do you want the recipient to be able to download the attached file?
questions.why: The Google Drive preview window shows a 'Download' button, indicating the current permissions allow the recipient to save the file locally.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the ability to control the specific access and download permissions for the file they are sharing.
questions.check: Does the file preview show a download option under the current permissions?
questions.say_example: Left downloading on, so <name> can save a copy.

questions.question: Which Google account do you want to use to sign in to Yahoo Mail?
questions.why: The screen prompts you to "Choose an account" to "continue to Yahoo!", which determines the sender identity for your email.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to ensure the email is sent from your preferred primary account rather than an alternate or work account.
questions.check: Which accounts does the account-chooser dialog list?
questions.say_example: Yahoo wants one of your Google accounts to sign in with. It lists <two>. Which one, or neither?

questions.question: Should I grant Yahoo permission to access and modify my Google Drive files?
questions.why: The authorization screen warns that Yahoo will be able to see, edit, create, and delete all of your Google Drive files.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the chance to evaluate whether they trust the email client with extensive access to their personal cloud storage.
questions.check: What access does the authorization screen say will be granted?
questions.say_example: To attach from Drive, <Yahoo> wants standing access to everything in your Drive. See, edit, and delete, all files, not just this one, and it stays after this email. Grant it, or send the file another way?

questions.question: Should I insert the file as a Drive link or as a direct attachment?
questions.why: The file selection modal provides 'Insert as' options at the bottom right to send either a Drive link or an actual Attachment.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to choose the most accessible file delivery method for your specific recipient.
questions.check: Which insert option is selected, Drive link or attachment?
questions.say_example: Attached a real copy rather than a link. Nothing for <name> to sign in for.

questions.question: Has the file finished uploading to the email draft?
questions.why: Sending the email before the progress bar for the zip file disappears could result in the message going out without the attachment.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the visual confirmation that your specific file successfully uploaded without errors before the message was sent.
questions.check: Does the attachment area still show an upload progress bar?
questions.say_example: The attachment's still uploading. I'll wait. Sending now would drop it.

children.label: Send or save the message
children.note: 6.1 first in the keepers that check anything. then exactly one of 6.2 to 6.5 - the four ways a draft ends here. 6.6 where the client refuses to proceed as-is. 6.7 when a cloud attachment forces a second commit before delivery. 6.8 to read whatever comes back. eight keepers produce no evidenced commit at all.

questions.question: Do the links in the draft exactly match the ones in the source document?
questions.why: The screen showed different video IDs in the final Gmail draft compared to the original Google Doc.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the assurance that the correct information is being sent to the recipient when the agent alters or miscopies the provided links.
questions.check: Does each link in the draft match, character for character, the link in the source it was copied from?
questions.say_example: One link didn't survive the paste. It points somewhere different from the doc, so I put the doc's version back.

questions.question: Are there any red squiggly lines or visual spell-check indicators under the text you just pasted or typed?
questions.why: Email clients visually flag typos and grammar errors in real-time, allowing quick corrections before the message is sent.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the passive visual safety net of native spell-check indicators, risking sending an unprofessional email if the agent ignores them.
questions.check: Does the body show spell-check underlines, and under which words?
questions.say_example: Spell-check flagged <two> words, <'recieve'> and <'thier'>. Want them fixed before it goes?

questions.question: Is the file on the attachment chip the one you meant to send?
questions.why: The screen displays an attachment card for 'Pond.jpg' with a thumbnail and file size that needs verification before addressing the email.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the ability to visually verify the attachment thumbnail and file size before the agent proceeds to draft and send the email.
questions.check: What file name and size does the attachment chip show?
questions.say_example: The chip says <IMG_2041.jpg>, but you asked for <the resume>. Swapping it before this goes anywhere.

questions.question: Do you see the same file size for the attachment in your draft as you did in the file browser?
questions.why: Confirming that the '36 KB' size of the attached 'Main Resume.docx' matches the iOS file browser ensures the correct document was successfully uploaded.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the opportunity to manually cross-reference file metadata to guarantee the right document is being sent.
questions.check: Does the size on the attachment chip match the size the file picker showed for that file?
questions.say_example: The attached file shows <36 KB> but the one you picked was <3 MB>. That may be the wrong file or a broken upload. Checking before send.

questions.question: Does the greeting in the email body match the recipient's email address?
questions.why: The recipient field shows [email], but the message body addresses 'James', indicating a mismatch before sending.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user risks sending an email to the wrong person or confusing the recipient with an incorrect greeting.
questions.check: What name does the greeting use, and what name is in the recipient's address?
questions.say_example: The message opens with <Hi James> but it's addressed to <mary.smith@...>. Right person?

questions.question: Ready to send — recipient, subject, message, and attachment all as you want them?
questions.why: The compose window shows 'Cool Guy.jpg' successfully attached at the bottom, indicating the message is complete and ready for dispatch.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the final opportunity to verify that the correct file was attached before the email is irreversibly sent.
questions.check: What do the To, Cc, Subject, and attachment fields show, and which account is sending?
questions.say_example: Ready to send. To <name>, subject <subject>, with <the file> attached, from <your address>. Want me to read the message first? Press to send, or say change.

questions.question: What date and time should I schedule this email to send?
questions.why: The 'Pick date & time' dialog requires a specific calendar day and time to ensure the message arrives exactly when intended.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this means you lose the ability to strategically time the email's arrival, such as right before a scheduled meeting.
questions.check: What date and time does the schedule dialog show?
questions.say_example: Scheduled for <tomorrow at 8>, like you asked.

questions.question: Should you check 'Don't show again' before clicking 'Got it' on the junk mail warning?
questions.why: The dialog box offers a choice to permanently dismiss future warnings about email best practices by checking a box before proceeding.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the ability to decide whether they want to be reminded of email best practices in the future.
questions.check: Does the dialog offer a 'Don't show again' checkbox?
questions.say_example: Dismissed the warning for this send only. Future warnings stay on.

questions.question: Should you send a preview email to yourself before sending it to the whole list?
questions.why: The 'Ready to send' dialog offers a 'Send preview' option to verify the formatting before dispatching the separate emails to your recipients.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Letting an agent automatically skip the preview removes your final chance to catch formatting errors or mistakes before the emails reach your recipients.
questions.check: Does the send dialog offer a preview option, and how many recipients does it say the batch will go to?
questions.say_example: Before this goes to <30> people, want a preview copy in your own inbox first?

questions.question: Does the number of selected contacts match the number of emails shown in the send confirmation?
questions.why: Verifying that the '3 selected' contacts matches the '3 separate emails will be sent' message ensures the system correctly registered your intended recipients.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the final safety check that prevents accidentally emailing the wrong number of people before the messages actually go out.
questions.check: What recipient count does the send confirmation state, and how many contacts were selected?
questions.say_example: You picked <3> people but it's about to send <4> emails. Holding until those match.

questions.question: Do you want to send this email without a subject?
questions.why: The mail client displayed a 'Missing subject' warning, requiring a choice between sending the email as-is or returning to the draft to add one.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this choice means losing the opportunity to decide whether a blank subject line is acceptable for this specific recipient or if it looks too unprofessional.
questions.check: Does the client show a missing-subject warning?
questions.say_example: There's no subject on this. Send it bare, or tell me what to put?

questions.question: Did the mail client display a 'forgot attachment' warning when you clicked send?
questions.why: If you typed words like 'attached' in the body but haven't actually attached a file, mail clients often catch the error and ask for confirmation before sending.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the safety net of the system's attachment reminder, risking the agent blindly clicking 'Send anyway' and delivering an incomplete message.
questions.check: Does the client show a warning that the message mentions an attachment but has none?
questions.say_example: The client noticed the message says 'attached' but nothing is. Add the file, or send as is?

questions.question: How should you set the access permissions for the linked Google Drive file?
questions.why: The dialog requires choosing between restricting access to specific people or allowing anyone with the link to view the file.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose control over balancing file security against the recipient's convenience when accessing the attachment.
questions.check: Which access options does the sharing dialog offer, and which is selected?
questions.say_example: The link needs a setting. Just <name>, or anyone who has the link? Anyone-with-the-link stays open to whoever it gets forwarded to.

questions.question: Do you see a 'Sending...' notification confirming the action is in progress?
questions.why: The black 'Sending...' toast at the bottom of the inbox screen confirms the app registered the send command and is actively processing the email.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: An agent might close the app immediately after clicking send rather than waiting for completion, which could interrupt the process and leave the email stuck in the outbox.
questions.check: Does the page show a 'Sending...' toast?
questions.say_example: The send is in motion.

questions.question: Did you see the 'Message sent' confirmation banner?
questions.why: The bottom-left banner changing from 'Sending...' to 'Message sent' confirms the email was successfully dispatched.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this means you miss the brief window to click 'Undo' if you suddenly realize you made a mistake in the email.
questions.check: Does the page show the 'Message sent' confirmation, and is an Undo option still visible?
questions.say_example: Sent, <3:07>. You can still say undo for the next <10> seconds.

children.label: Confirm the message went
children.note: 7.1 first - the toast is not treated as sufficient, and three keepers open the folder straight after seeing one. 7.2 when the message is not where it should be. 7.3 where the client filed it somewhere else. 7.4 in the six keepers that go and look at the receiving end. seven keepers stop at the toast or before it.

questions.question: Did a bounce-back arrive saying the message could not be delivered?
questions.why: If an email address is mistyped or the recipient's inbox is full, the mail server will immediately return a failure notification, meaning the email must be corrected and resent.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the immediate feedback loop of catching a delivery failure, potentially believing a critical email was received when it actually bounced.
questions.check: Did a 'Message not delivered' or mail-delivery-failure message arrive in the inbox?
questions.say_example: It bounced. <The address> couldn't be reached, so <name> never got it. Want to check the address and resend?

questions.question: Is this message in the Sent folder?
questions.why: Checking the Sent folder after seeing the 'Message sent' notification confirms that the message and its attachments were actually dispatched.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the peace of mind of visually confirming that the exact message and its attachments are safely logged in your sent history.
questions.check: Does the Sent folder show the message at the top?
questions.say_example: It's in Sent, <3:07>.

questions.question: Are the recipient, subject, body, and attachment correct in the sent message?
questions.why: Reviewing the sent message details, including the recipient, text, and image thumbnail, confirms the email was transmitted exactly as intended.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the peace of mind of personally confirming that the correct message and file actually went to the right person.
questions.check: Do the sent copy's recipient, subject, and attachment match what was approved at the send gate?
questions.say_example: The sent copy doesn't match what you approved. It went out without the attachment. Want me to send a follow-up with the file?

questions.question: Are you verifying the sent email in the same account you used to draft it?
questions.why: The email was drafted from [email], but the Sent folder shown later belongs to [email] and does not contain the drafted message.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user cannot confirm if their email was actually sent because the agent checked the wrong account's Sent folder.
questions.check: Which account's Sent folder is currently displayed?
questions.say_example: I couldn't find it in Sent at first. I was looking in the wrong account. It's there in <the right one>.

questions.question: Is there an 'Offline' or 'Working Offline' indicator visible in the mail client interface?
questions.why: If the device or client has lost connection, the email will be queued in the outbox rather than sent immediately, changing whether the user should expect an immediate reply.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the awareness that their message will be delayed until the connection is restored, falsely believing it was sent instantly.
questions.check: Does the client show an offline or working-offline indicator?
questions.say_example: You're offline, so the email is waiting in the outbox. It goes the moment the connection's back.

questions.question: Did your email send, or is it stuck in the outbox?
questions.why: The Sent folder did not show the recent email and instead displayed a banner for unsent messages in the Outbox, indicating a delivery issue that needs to be investigated.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the certainty of knowing whether your message actually reached the recipient or if it silently failed to send.
questions.check: Does the outbox show the message still queued or uploading?
questions.say_example: It said sending, but the message is actually still in the outbox, stuck on the attachment. I'll watch it and tell you if it doesn't go.

questions.question: Is your email correctly queued in the Scheduled folder with the right contents?
questions.why: Checking the Scheduled folder and the banner inside the email confirms your message is queued to go out at the exact time you intended.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the peace of mind of personally verifying the scheduled time and contents before the delayed send occurs.
questions.check: Does the Scheduled folder show the message with the chosen send time?
questions.say_example: It's queued. Going out <tomorrow at 8>. You can still change or cancel it there.

children.label: Check the receiving end
children.note: 7.4.1, then 7.4.2 where it has not landed yet, then 7.4.3. 7.4.4 where the point of the message was the file.

questions.question: Do you see the new email in the inbox?
questions.why: The screen shows a new email from 'me' with the subject 'Leave letter', confirming the message was delivered.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the immediate reassurance of personally verifying that the email successfully reached its destination.
questions.check: Does the inbox show the new message with the expected subject?
questions.say_example: Your own copy arrived, so the send is confirmed.

questions.question: Does the shared link open without requiring sign-in?
questions.why: The screen shows the recipient clicking the Google Drive link in the email to confirm the file opens successfully without requiring a login.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the peace of mind of manually testing the link to ensure the recipient will not face permission errors.
questions.check: Does the shared link open the file without asking for sign-in or access?
questions.say_example: The link asks for permission when opened outside your account, so <name> would hit a locked door. Loosen the sharing, or attach the file instead?

questions.question: Did the mail merge correctly populate the recipient's name in the greeting?
questions.why: Checking that the email body starts with the actual name confirms the mail merge tag successfully pulled the recipient's information instead of sending a broken placeholder.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this check means you lose the peace of mind of confirming your automated greetings look professional rather than exposing raw merge tags to your recipients.
questions.check: Does the preview copy's greeting show a real name rather than a literal tag or a blank?
questions.say_example: In the preview, the greeting came out as <@firstname>, not a name. The merge isn't pulling the sheet, so I'm holding the batch.

questions.question: Does the attachment size in the received email match the size shown when you attached it?
questions.why: The attached 'Password 123.txt' file displays a size of 1K in the Gmail compose window but 59B in the received Yahoo email, suggesting a potential inconsistency.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses confidence that the exact file they attached was transmitted without alteration or data loss.
questions.check: What size does the received copy show for the attachment?
questions.say_example: The received copy shows the attachment at <59 B> against <1 K> attached. That's display rounding, same file.

questions.question: Did the forwarded email arrive with only your new message and no previous history?
questions.why: The recipient's inbox shows the email from 'Woggle Guides', and opening it confirms the body only contains 'My goofy cat!' and the image without the original email trail.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the peace of mind of personally verifying that unnecessary email history was successfully scrubbed before the recipient saw it.
questions.check: Does the received copy's body contain only the new message, without the quoted thread?
questions.say_example: The forward went with just your note, no old thread attached.

questions.question: Has the download finished, or is it still in progress?
questions.why: The screen shows the notification shade pulled down over a received email to check for a download confirmation.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the ability to confirm that the required file was successfully saved to the device before attempting to attach it.
questions.check: Does the notification shade show the download in progress?
questions.say_example: The download started. It's in your notifications.

children.label: Handle a received message
children.note: 8.1 to open it - and on the reply and forward routes this is where the task begins, running straight into 2.2. 8.2 where the thread hides part of itself. 8.3 to see who else is on it. 8.4 to 8.8 in any order and almost entirely in one keeper, which files, stars, snoozes and un-reads a single message and then puts every one of them back.

questions.question: Which email thread should you open to forward?
questions.why: The inbox displays numerous messages, and clicking the 'Welcome to the weekend!' thread dictates the specific content to be forwarded.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses control over selecting the exact historical context or conversation to share with the new recipient.
questions.check: Which threads in the inbox match the message the person described?
questions.say_example: Two threads match <'weekend'>, one from <[name]>, one from <Woggle Guides>. Which one?

questions.question: Which specific email in the thread do you want to forward?
questions.why: The expanded thread shows multiple messages, such as the ones from [name] at 6:14 AM and Woggle Guides at 6:20 AM, and you must select the exact one containing the picture you want to share.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to personally select which specific message and context from the ongoing conversation gets forwarded to your friend.
questions.check: How many messages does the expanded thread contain, and which matches the person's description?
questions.say_example: This thread has <six> messages. I'd forward <the 6:20 one with the picture>. That the one?

questions.question: Who exactly is included in the To and Cc fields on this thread?
questions.why: Expanding the collapsed header reveals the specific sender and all Cc'd parties, ensuring you know exactly who will receive your message if you reply all.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The delegator loses direct visibility into the specific individuals included in the conversation, risking unintended sharing of information with hidden recipients.
questions.check: Which addresses does the expanded thread header list in To and Cc?
questions.say_example: The thread header lists <four> people in all.
